previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with hypertension and acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, presenting with chest pressure, worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and fluid overload. She had recently stopped her diuretics (torsemide and spironolactone) after a prior admission for hyperkalemia and kidney injury, which contributed to her decompensation. IV Lasix was given, resulting in significant diuresis and clinical improvement. Her blood pressure was initially managed with nitroprusside but was stabilized on oral medications, including a switch from metoprolol to carvedilol for better heart failure control. Troponins were negative, ruling out acute coronary syndrome. Potassium was treated with Kayexalate and normalized. She was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved symptoms, and instructions to monitor weight and continue her medications, including restarting torsemide and adhering to a low-sodium diet.

# Delirium: Likely multifactorial given recent surgery, 
hospitalization, pain medications, and possibly uremia. Pain

 The urine culture grew pseudomonas aeruginos sensitive to cipro

Pt also with anxiety and concern for mental status throughout

# Acute on chronic renal failure:  ___ Crt 2.5-2.9. Her Cr 
had been trending up since surgery. Obstructive etiologies ruled 
out with renal U/S. Nephrology was consulted, who felt that 
granular casts, hyaline casts, and tubular epithelial cells seen 
on sediment could be the result of fluctuating BPs or mild ATN.  
It is thought that perhaps the amount of fluid she received led 
to acute exacerbation of dCHF, leading to poor forward flow. She 
was initially started on IV lasix for diuresis per renal recs, 
and her Cr began to improve. On ___, the patient's UOP dropped 
despite furosemide gtt and 80 torsemide PO. This also proved 
refractory to another 80 torsemide and 25 chlorthalidone. A 
temporary dialysis catheter was placed on ___ and she was 
started on CVVH for volume overload. Patient was called out of

was continued on HD and a tunneled HD line was placed on ___

D repletion. 
PPD placed in house was negative.

# Acute on chronic diastolic CHF: Pt was grossly fluid 
overloaded in the FICU. Echo showed normal EF without wall 
motion abnormality.  Previous chest imaging showed cardiomegaly. 
Likely a diastolic component of CHF. CXR was consistent with 
pulmonary vascular congestion as well and pt was initially 
hypoxic in the ICU. Pt was diuresed with IV lasix until HD was 
started.  The patient underwent HD with good effect and improved 
respiratory status. She was placed on Metoprolol (held on HD 
days given low BP). Pt's weight on discharge was 119.2kg. 

# S/p right total knee replacement & persistent knee pain: 
Elective surgery on ___. Patient continued to have significant 
pain despite pain medication.  Patient received SQH TID for

control improved with standing tylenol and low dose oxycodone 
prn. She will follow-up with orthopedics as an outpatient on 
___. 

# Anemia, normocytic:  Chronic in nature.  Baseline Hct usually 
in the ___.  Most likely has some degree of anemia from 
chronic kidney disease which is now worsened by acute on chronic 
KD and recent acute blood loss from TKR. Her Hct was monitored 
with a transfusion threshold of 21. Her stools (x3) were 
hemoccult negative. On ___, patient received 1u pRBC during 
CVVH.  She was given an additional unit of blood on ___. She 
was started on iron with HD.

by nonhealing sternal incision wound, MI in ___ and ___. Pt

tunneled line, and continued to hold on discharge in 
anticipation of AV graft procedure as discussed above. She was 
continued on metoprolol, rosuvastatin, and isosorbide. Her

# Thrombocytopenia: Mild drop to 130s, low concern for HIT given

INDICATION:  End-stage renal disease, tunneled line requested.

PHYSICIAN:  ___, M.D., fellow, performed the procedure.  ___,
M.D., attending, was present and supervising the procedure.

MEDICATIONS:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
fentanyl totaling 75 mcg and Versed totaling 1.5 mg throughout the total
intraservice time of 30 minutes, during which the patient's hemodynamic
parameters were continuously monitored.

PROCEDURES:  Conversion of temporary right IJ hemodialysis line to a tunneled
line.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  Informed consent was obtained.  The patient was positioned
supine.  The area was prepped and draped in sterile fashion.  Timeout was
performed.  Fluoroscopy was used intermittently.

Local anesthesia was applied.  A ___ wire was placed through the indwelling
dialysis catheter into the inferior vena cava.  This was used to measure the
distance to the planned tunnel exit site.  The indwelling catheter was
removed.  Unfortunately, the wire access was inadvertently lost at this point.
Pressure was held for good hemostasis.  With ultrasound guidance and
micropuncture technique, the right internal jugular vein was re-accessed.  The
tract was first dilated with a micropuncture sheath.  A ___ wire was then
advanced into the inferior vena cava.  The chosen tunnel exit site was
anesthetized.  The tunnel was then anesthetized and dissected with lidocaine
plus epinephrine.  The catheter was flushed and soaked in antibiotic solution.
It was then tunneled subcutaneously to exit at the venotomy site.  Serial
dilators were then passed at the venotomy site into the vein followed by the
peel-away sheath.  Through the peel-away sheath, the catheter tip was pushed
into the right atrium.  The peel-away sheath was removed.  The catheter was
affixed to the skin with suture and covered with an appropriate dressing.  The
venotomy site was closed with ___ Vicryl absorbable sutures and covered with a
dressing.  Both lumens aspirated and flushed easily.  Heparin was left to
dwell in the line per protocol.  There were no complications.  This is a 23-cm
tip-to-cuff length hemodialysis catheter.

CONCLUSION:  Uncomplicated placement of a tunneled hemodialysis catheter, 23
cm tip-to-cuff, with tip in the right atrium.
